title: The Mel Blanc Show
paragraphs: One-season CBS situation comedy starring Mel Blanc as a fictionalized Fix-It Shop owner. 14/Jan.
The run breaks into several distinct periods: CBS / Colgate run (September 3, 1946 to June 24, 1947) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Mel Blanc (performer), Mary Jane Croft (performer), Victor Miller and His Orchestra (performer), Joseph Kearns (performer), Bud Hiestand (announcer), Hans Conried (performer), and The Sportsmen (performer).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

The stories often return to fix-it shop and repair-business comedy, Mel and Betty romance/engagement, Mr. Colby conflict and future in-laws, holiday and seasonal comedy, show business, movies and performers, and Loyal Order of Benevolent Zebras and lodge comedy.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Competing collector chronology traditions, Postwar network situation comedy, Voice performer as radio sitcom star, and Colgate-sponsored commercial radio.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|the-phil-harris-alice-faye-show|The Phil Harris-Alice Faye Show]], [[show|the-railroad-hour|The Railroad Hour]], [[show|fibber-mcgee-and-molly|Fibber McGee and Molly]], and [[show|my-favorite-husband|My Favorite Husband]].
